questions.explain: Showback tells teams what they would be charged (informational, dashboard only) while chargeback actually moves the money into their budget (Finance/procurement involved) — but both require identical infrastructure: cost data, tag coverage, allocation rules, pipelines. Start with showback but build the infrastructure for chargeback from day one (retrofitting allocation logic later is painful); formal models cut spend 20–35% within two quarters.
options: Showback = informational allocation (dashboard), chargeback = real money movement (Finance/procurement); same infrastructure either way — start with showback but build for chargeback from day one; models cut spend 20–35% in two quarters
Showback and chargeback are the same thing

questions.explain: Three strategies: equal split (simple, inaccurate, politically acceptable because equally wrong), weighted by consumption metric (storage, CPU seconds, query count — more accurate but needs instrumentation), direct assignment (clean accounting but causes sprawl and kills economies of scale). Most mature organizations use a hybrid: direct for dedicated instances, weighted for shared clusters, with periodic review for allocation drift.
options: Equal split, weighted-by-consumption, and direct assignment — mature orgs use a hybrid: direct for dedicated instances, weighted for shared clusters, with periodic drift review
Shared infrastructure should never be allocated

questions.explain: Minimum viable tag set: Environment, Team, Application, CostCenter, Owner — coverage below 90% makes any allocation model politically fragile, since teams can credibly dispute with 'we couldn't tag that resource', so drive to 98%+ before launching chargeback. Note gaps: AWS doesn't tag snapshots/backups by default, Azure doesn't tag bandwidth charges, and GCP labels differ in billing exports.
options: Environment/Team/Application/CostCenter/Owner minimum; below 90% coverage allocation is politically fragile — reach 98%+ before chargeback; handle AWS snapshot/AZ bandwidth/GCP label gaps explicitly
questions.q: What tag coverage foundation does cost allocation need?

questions.explain: For shared databases, meter consumption via Query Store/dm_exec_query_stats windowed to the billing cycle (team CPU seconds, IO weight), using a blended weight like 60% CPU + 40% IO. Critical discipline: never run SET QUERY_STORE CLEAR for billing windows — it destroys the historical baseline; filter sys.query_store_runtime_stats_interval on billing boundaries instead.
options: Meter shared databases with Query Store windowed to the billing cycle (blended 60% CPU + 40% IO weight); never CLEAR Query Store — filter runtime stats intervals by billing window
questions.q: How do you meter shared databases for accurate allocation?

questions.explain: Disputes almost always come from three causes: another team reduced their consumption (shifting relative weights), a batch job ran outside its normal window, or a shared resource was resized changing the base cost. Build dispute resolution in from the start with a month-over-month allocation-change audit query that resolves 90% of disputes without escalation.
options: Disputes are usually caused by another team's reduced consumption shifting weights, an off-window batch job, or a shared resource resize — resolve with a month-over-month allocation-change audit
